docs.title: STL map and multimap
docs.text:
map/multimap use rb_tree as their underlying structure, and therefore have the characteristic of automatic element sorting, with sorting based on the key.

map/multimap provide "traversal" operations and iterators. Traversing by the normal rules (++iter) yields the sorted order.

We cannot use map/multimap iterators to change an element's key (because the key has its strict ordering rules), but we can use them to change the element's data. Therefore map/multimap internally automatically sets the user-specified key type to const, thereby forbidding users from assigning to an element's key.

The key of a map element must be unique, so its insert uses the rb_tree's _M_insert_unique(), while the key of a multimap element may repeat, so its insert uses the rb_tree's _M_insert_equal().

In this section we will cover the following:

  • map's key is the key and its value is key+data, which differs from set, where the key is the value and the value is the key.
  • map's key cannot be modified; map and multimap call different insertion functions, which affects whether a key maps to multiple values.
  • initializer_list usage
  • map has the [] operator, while multimap does not have a [] operator.

docs.title: 1.map
docs.text:
the key is the key, the value is key+data

In the map below we can see that value_type is a pair.

template <typename _Key, typename _Tp, typename _Compare = std::less<_Key>,
typename _Alloc = std::allocator<std::pair<const _Key, _Tp> > >
class map
{
public:
    typedef _Key                                          key_type;
    typedef _Tp                                           mapped_type;
    typedef std::pair<const _Key, _Tp>                    value_type;
    typedef _Compare                                      key_compare;
    typedef _Alloc                                        allocator_type;
private:
    // key​为​key,value​为​key+data
    typedef _Rb_tree<key_type, value_type, _Select1st<value_type>,
            key_compare, _Pair_alloc_type> _Rep_type;

    /// The actual tree structure.
    _Rep_type _M_t;
};

The default functor above is _Select1st; in stl_function we see the following source:

template<typename _Pair>
struct _Select1st
: public unary_function<_Pair, typename _Pair::first_type>
{
    typename _Pair::first_type&
    operator()(_Pair& __x) const
    { return __x.first; }
};
We see that _Select1st above is a struct — how can we call it a functor? Because it overloads a () operator, haha~

Now let's implement one ourselves:

template<typename _T1>
struct mySelect1st
        : public unary_function<_T1, typename _T1::first_type>
{
    template<typename _T2>
    typename _T2::first_type&
    operator()(_T2& __x) const
    { return __x.first; }
};
int main() {
     typedef pair<const int,int> value_type;
    _Rb_tree<int, value_type, mySelect1st<value_type>, less<int>> it;
    it._M_insert_unique(make_pair(1,3));
    it._M_insert_unique(make_pair(3,6));
    for(auto each:it)
        cout<<each.first<<" "<<each.second<<endl;
}

the key cannot be modified, the data can

In the source above, a const is automatically added to the key, so the key cannot be modified. 

typedef std::pair<const _Key, _Tp>                    value_type;

docs.title: 2.insert
docs.text:
insert uses _M_insert_unique

The several insert methods:

(1) Insert a pair

std::pair<iterator, bool> insert(const value_type& __x)
{ return _M_t._M_insert_unique(__x); }

inside map

(2) Insert a pair at a specified position 

iterator insert(iterator __position, const value_type& __x)
{ return _M_t._M_insert_equal_(__position, __x); }

(3) Insert from a range

template<typename _InputIterator>
void
insert(_InputIterator __first, _InputIterator __last)
{ _M_t._M_insert_equal(__first, __last); }
(4) Insert from a list

void
insert(initializer_list<value_type> __l)
{ this->insert(__l.begin(), __l.end()); }

For the last insert, there is an initializer_list; an example will make it clear.

docs.title: 3.initializer_list usage
docs.text:
Hands-on practice

vector<int> v={1,2,3};   // ​底层​调用​vector​的​构造函数​
v={2,5,6};               // ​底层​调用​vector​的​=​操作符​
initializer_list<int> ll={4,5,6};
v.insert(v.begin(),ll);  // ​底层​调用​下面​insert​函数​
for(auto x:v) cout<<x<<" ";
cout<<endl;
vector<int> vv(ll);      // ​底层​调用​vector​的​构造函数​
vector<string> city{"Berlin", "New York", "London", "Cairo","Tokyo", "Cologne"};
Everyone is very familiar with this vector initialization — why can it be initialized this way? Let's look at the vector source code:

 vector&
operator=(initializer_list<value_type> __l)
{
    this->assign(__l.begin(), __l.end());
    return *this;
}

iterator
insert(const_iterator __position, initializer_list<value_type> __l)
{ return this->insert(__position, __l.begin(), __l.end()); }

vector(initializer_list<value_type> __l,
const allocator_type& __a = allocator_type())
: _Base(__a)
{
_M_range_initialize(__l.begin(), __l.end(),
    random_access_iterator_tag());
}

Because its constructor has an initializer_list parameter, we can apply this to map. But map has no analogous constructor; it is applied in map's constructor, insert, and = — the same three places as above, haha~

Three places where initializer_list is used:

// map​构造​
map(initializer_list<value_type> __l, const allocator_type& __a)
: _M_t(_Compare(), _Pair_alloc_type(__a))
{ _M_t._M_insert_unique(__l.begin(), __l.end()); }
// =​操作符​重载​
map&
operator=(initializer_list<value_type> __l)
{
    this->clear();
    this->insert(__l.begin(), __l.end());
    return *this;
}
// insert​插入​
void
insert(std::initializer_list<value_type> __list)
{ insert(__list.begin(), __list.end()); }

Hands-on practice

Using initializer_list with map (used the same way with set):

// ​这里​要​注意​，pair​的​first​参数​必​[​须​是​const
initializer_list<pair<const strin[g,int>> l = {{"hello", 1}, {"world", 2}};
map<string,int> mm(l);  // map​构造函数​
map<string, int> m2{{"hello", 1}, {"world", 2}}; // map​构造函数​
map<string, int> m1={{"hello", 1}, {"world", 2}};   // map​构造函数​
m1 = {{"h", 1}, {"w", 3}};             // ​底层​调用​map​的​=​操作符​
map<string, int> mp;
mp.insert(l);       // insert​插入​[
The above raises another question:

map<string, int> m1={{"hello", 1}, {"world", 2}};   // map​构造函数​
m1 = {{"h", 1}, {"w", 3}};             // ​底层​调用​map​的​=​操作符​
Why does one of these two call the constructor and the other the = operator?

At initialization time, when defining and assigning in one go, the constructor is called directly; a later re-assignment first calls the copy constructor (which may be optimized away by the compiler) and then the = operator.

Example analysis

Let's analyze it with a concrete example:

template <typename _Tp>
class Foo
{
public:
    Foo(initializer_list<_Tp> &list)
    {
        cout << "Foo(initializer_list<_Tp> &list)"<< endl;
    }

    Foo(int)
    {
        cout << "Foo(int )"<< endl;
    }

    Foo(const Foo& f)
    {
        cout << "​调用​了​拷贝​构造函数​"<< endl;
    }
    Foo& operator=(initializer_list<_Tp> __l)
    {
        cout<<"​调用​了​=​操作符​重载​"<<endl;
        return *this;
    }

};
Called with: 
Foo<int> foo=ll;
foo={1,2};
Result with the compiler unoptimized:

Foo(initializer_list<_Tp> &list)
​调用​了​=​操作符​重载​
By disabling compiler optimization: g++ -o rb rbtree.cpp -std=c++11 -fno-elide-constructors

Foo(initializer_list<_Tp> &list)
​调用​了​拷贝​构造函数​
​调用​了​=​操作符​重载​

docs.title: 4.multimap
docs.text:
Like map, multimap does not allow modifying the key. But its insertion uses _M_insert_equal. 

template <typename _Key, typename _Tp,
typename _Compare = std::less<_Key>,
typename _Alloc = std::allocator<std::pair<const _Key, _Tp> > >
class multimap
{
public:                                      
    typedef std::pair<const _Key, _Tp> value_type;   
}
Below we practice with multimap and rbtree in two ways. 
multimap<int, string> c;
c.insert(make_pair(1,"asdqw"));
c.insert(make_pair(1,"qweq"));

for(auto each:c) cout<<each.first<<" "<<each.second<<endl;

typedef pair<const int,string> valueT;
_Rb_tree<int, valueT, _Select1st<valueT>, less<int>> mulm;
mulm._M_insert_equal(make_pair(2,"abc"));
mulm._M_insert_equal(make_pair(2,"cde"));
for(auto each:mulm)
cout<<each.first<<" "<<each.second<<endl;
Output:

1 asdqw
1 qweq
2 abc
2 cde

docs.title: 5.Important operators of map and multimap
docs.text:
For the [] operator of map and multimap: map's [] operator returns the second parameter passed to the map.

Pass a key to []; if it is found, you get the value, otherwise the default value 0. 

mapped_type&
operator[](const key_type& __k)
{
    iterator __i = lower_bound(__k);// ​找到​__k​第一个​。
    // __i->first is greater than or equivalent to __k.
    if (__i == end() || key_comp()(__k, (*__i).first))
    #if __cplusplus >= 201103L
    __i = _M_t._M_emplace_hint_unique(__i, std::piecewise_construct,
                    std::tuple<const key_type&>(__k),
                    std::tuple<>());
    #else
        __i = insert(__i, value_type(__k, mapped_type()));
    #endif
    return (*__i).second;  // ​返回​key​的​value，​此​value​为​传递​进​map​的​第二个​参数​。
}

But multimap has no [] operator!!!

Let's think about it: since a multimap key may correspond to multiple values, if we fetched the value for a key via [], which value would we actually get? That is why the STL source code does not overload this operator!

docs.title: STL queue and stack source code analysis
0.Introduction
docs.text:
Why are stack and queue not called containers?

In this section we dive into the source code analysis with this question in mind.

docs.title: 1.stack
docs.text:
In the source code of stack we focus on two points: - the default _Sequence is deque - the internal function implementations call the corresponding functions of the _Sequence container.

template<typename _Tp, typename _Sequence = deque<_Tp> >
class stack
{

public:
    typedef typename _Sequence::value_type                value_type;
    typedef typename _Sequence::reference                 reference;
    typedef typename _Sequence::const_reference           const_reference;
    typedef typename _Sequence::size_type                 size_type;
    typedef          _Sequence                            container_type;

protected:
    //  See queue::c for notes on this name.
    _Sequence c;

public:
     reference
      top()
      {
        __glibcxx_requires_nonempty();
        return c.back();
      }
    void
      push(const value_type& __x)
      { c.push_back(__x); }
}

Testing the underlying container of stack

For stack, the underlying container can be vector, deque, or list, but not map or set. Since the compiler does not perform a comprehensive check, compilation fails only when a called function does not exist; so although something like set cannot serve as the underlying container, if it happens to have certain functions the calls still succeed — until a called function does not exist.

int test_stack() {
    cout<<"============test_stack============="<<endl;
    clock_t timeStart = clock();
    stack<int, list<int>> c;
    for (long i = 0; i < 100000; i++)
        c.push(i+1);
    cout << "stack.size()= " << c.size() << endl;
    cout << "stack.top()= " << c.top() << endl;
    c.pop();
    cout << "stack.size()= " << c.size() << endl;
    cout << "stack.top()= " << c.top() << endl;
    cout << "use stack milli-seconds : " << (clock() - timeStart) << endl;
    timeStart=clock();
    stack<int, deque<int>> c1;
    for (long i = 0; i < 100000; i++)
        c1.push(i+1);
    cout << "stack.size()= " << c1.size() << endl;
    cout << "stack.top()= " << c1.top() << endl;
    c1.pop();
    cout << "stack.size()= " << c1.size() << endl;
    cout << "stack.top()= " << c1.top() << endl;
    cout << "use stack milli-seconds : " << (clock() - timeStart) << endl;

    // vector​可以​作为​stack​的​底层​容器​
    stack<int, vector<int>> c2;
    for (long i = 0; i < 100000; i++)
        c2.push(i+1);
    cout << "stack.size()= " << c2.size() << endl;
    cout << "stack.top()= " << c2.top() << endl;
    c2.pop();
    cout << "stack.size()= " << c2.size() << endl;
    cout << "stack.top()= " << c2.top() << endl;
    cout << "use stack milli-seconds : " << (clock() - timeStart) << endl;
}

docs.title: 2.queue
docs.text:
In the source code of queue we focus on two points: - the default _Sequence is deque - the internal function implementations call the corresponding functions of the _Sequence container.

template<typename _Tp, typename _Sequence = deque<_Tp> >
class queue
{
public:
    typedef typename _Sequence::value_type                value_type;
    typedef typename _Sequence::reference                 reference;
    typedef typename _Sequence::const_reference           const_reference;
    typedef typename _Sequence::size_type                 size_type;
    typedef          _Sequence                            container_type;

protected:

    _Sequence c;

public:

    void push(const value_type& __x)
    { c.push_back(__x); }

    void pop()
    { 
        __glibcxx_requires_nonempty();
      c.pop_front();
    }
}
Its corresponding UML class diagram is as follows:

Similarly, the priority queue uses vector as its default container.

template<typename _Tp, typename _Sequence = vector<_Tp>,
typename _Compare  = less<typename _Sequence::value_type> >
class priority_queue
{
public:
    typedef typename _Sequence::value_type                value_type;
    typedef typename _Sequence::reference                 reference;
    typedef typename _Sequence::const_reference           const_reference;
    typedef typename _Sequence::size_type                 size_type;
    typedef          _Sequence                            container_type;

protected:
    //  See queue::c for notes on these names.
    _Sequence  c;
    _Compare   comp;

public:
    reference
    top() 
    {
        __glibcxx_requires_nonempty();
        return c.front();
    }

    void
    push(const value_type& __x)
    {
        c.push_back(__x);
        std::push_heap(c.begin(), c.end(), comp);
    }

}

Test the underlying containers supported by these two container adaptors:

queue

For queue the underlying container can be deque or list, but not vector, map, or set; using the default deque is faster at insertion than other containers as the underlying one!

int test_queue() {
    cout<<"============test_queue============="<<endl;
    clock_t timeStart = clock();
    queue<int, list<int>> c;
    for (long i = 0; i < 100000; i++) {
        c.push(i+1);
    }
    cout << "stack.size()= " << c.size() << endl;
    cout << "stack.front()= " << c.front() << endl;
    c.pop();
    cout << "stack.size()= " << c.size() << endl;
    cout << "stack.front()= " << c.front() << endl;
    cout << "use list milli-seconds : " << (clock() - timeStart) << endl;

    timeStart=clock();
    queue<int, deque<int>> c1;
    for (long i = 0; i < 100000; i++) {
        c1.push(i+1);
    }
    cout << "stack.size()= " << c1.size() << endl;
    cout << "stack.front()= " << c1.front() << endl;
    c1.pop();
    cout << "stack.size()= " << c1.size() << endl;
    cout << "stack.front()= " << c1.front() << endl;

    cout << "use deque milli-seconds : " << (clock() - timeStart) << endl;
}

priority_queue

For the priority queue, tests show that using deque is faster at insertion than the default vector! It supports vector and deque as the underlying containers, but not list, map, or set.

int test_priority_queue() {
    cout<<"============test_priority_queue============="<<endl;
    clock_t timeStart = clock();

    priority_queue<int, deque<int>> c1;
    for (long i = 0; i < 100000; i++) {
        c1.push(i+1);
    }
    cout << "stack.size()= " << c1.size() << endl;
    cout << "stack.top()= " << c1.top() << endl;
    c1.pop();
    cout << "stack.size()= " << c1.size() << endl;
    cout << "stack.top()= " << c1.top() << endl;

    cout << "use deque milli-seconds : " << (clock() - timeStart) << endl;


    priority_queue<int, vector<int>> c2;
    for (long i = 0; i < 100000; i++)
        c2.push(i+1);
    cout << "stack.size()= " << c2.size() << endl;
    cout << "stack.top()= " << c2.top() << endl;
    c2.pop();
    cout << "stack.size()= " << c2.size() << endl;
    cout << "stack.top()= " << c2.top() << endl;
    cout << "use stack milli-seconds : " << (clock() - timeStart) << endl;
}

Therefore, stack, queue, and priority_queue are not called containers; they are called container adaptors.

docs.title: STL red-black tree implementation | C++​那些​事
docs.text: Last updated：2026-10-13

docs.title: 0.Introduction
docs.text:
There are two passages in the STL source code, loosely translated as follows:

The Red-black tree class in the STL is used as the underlying structure of the STL associative containers (such as set, multiset, map, multimap). The insertion and deletion methods used inside are based on the book 《Introduction to Algorithms》, but with the following two differences:

(1) The header points not only to the root, but also to the leftmost node of the red-black tree, so that begin() can be implemented in constant time; it also points to the rightmost node of the red-black tree, so that set-related generic algorithms (such as set_union and so on) can achieve linear time performance.

(2) When the node to be deleted has two children, its successor node is linked into its position rather than copied; consequently, the only invalidated iterators are those referencing the deleted node.

The above, translated into a picture, is as follows: compared with an ordinary red-black tree there is an extra header node, and it is red. An ordinary red-black tree starts at node 100 and satisfies the following five properties: - Every node is either red or black. - The root is black. - Every leaf (NULL) is black. - If a node is red, then both its children are black. - For each node, all simple paths from the node to its descendant leaves contain the same number of black nodes.

Of course, this rb_tree likewise satisfies these properties; the iterator's begin points to the red-black tree's root — that is, the header's parent — while end points to the header node.

. The ellipsis in the figure means the nodes were not all drawn — other nodes exist, hence the omission.

docs.title: 1.Red-black tree node base class
docs.text:
The red-black tree base class is very simple; a color flag is defined at the start of the file.

The base class contains pointers to itself, defining left, right, and parent respectively, plus a color flag constant; inside there are two core functions whose purpose is to obtain the minimum and maximum nodes of the red-black tree. We know that for a binary search tree, obtaining the minimum node means searching down the left subtree continuously, and the maximum means searching down the right subtree.

// ​颜色​标记​
enum _Rb_tree_color { _S_red = false, _S_black = true };

// ​基类​
struct _Rb_tree_node_base
{
// typedef​重命名​
typedef _Rb_tree_node_base* _Base_ptr;

// ​颜色​
_Rb_tree_color  _M_color;
// ​指向​父亲​
_Base_ptr       _M_parent;
// ​指向​左​孩子​
_Base_ptr       _M_left;
// ​指向​右​孩子​
_Base_ptr       _M_right;

// ​求红​黑树​的​最小​节点​
static _Base_ptr
_S_minimum(_Base_ptr __x) _GLIBCXX_NOEXCEPT
{
    while (__x->_M_left != 0) __x = __x->_M_left;
    return __x;
}

// ​求红​黑树​最大​节点​
static _Base_ptr
_S_maximum(_Base_ptr __x) _GLIBCXX_NOEXCEPT
{
    while (__x->_M_right != 0) __x = __x->_M_right;
    return __x;
}

};

docs.title: 2.Red-black tree node
docs.text:
The red-black tree node inherits from the red-black tree base class. 

template<typename _Val>
struct _Rb_tree_node : public _Rb_tree_node_base
{
    typedef _Rb_tree_node<_Value>* _Link_type;//​节点​指针​,​指向​数据​节点​
    _Value _M_value_field;//​节点​数据​域​,​即​关键字​
};

docs.title: 3.Red-black tree iterator
docs.text:
Inside the red-black tree iterator there is a red-black tree base class member, through which the iterator's related operations are performed. At the same time, we can tell that this iterator is a bidirectional_iterator_tag.

It also contains the typedefs needed by the traits extractor.

template<typename _Tp>
struct _Rb_tree_iterator
{
    typedef _Tp  value_type;
    typedef _Tp& reference;
    typedef _Tp* pointer;

    typedef bidirectional_iterator_tag iterator_category;
    typedef ptrdiff_t                  difference_type;

    typedef _Rb_tree_iterator<_Tp>        _Self;
    typedef _Rb_tree_node_base::_Base_ptr _Base_ptr;
    typedef _Rb_tree_node<_Tp>*           _Link_type;

    _Base_ptr _M_node;
};

Getting the data

reference
operator*() const _GLIBCXX_NOEXCEPT
{ return *static_cast<_Link_type>(_M_node)->_M_valptr(); }

pointer
operator->() const _GLIBCXX_NOEXCEPT
{ return static_cast<_Link_type> (_M_node)->_M_valptr(); }

Overloading the ++ operator

_Self&
operator++() _GLIBCXX_NOEXCEPT
{
    _M_node = _Rb_tree_increment(_M_node);
    return *this;
}
And _Rb_tree_increment is backed by local_Rb_tree_increment, implemented as follows:

static _Rb_tree_node_base *
local_Rb_tree_increment( _Rb_tree_node_base* __x ) throw ()
{
    if ( __x->_M_right != 0 )       /* ​存在​右子​树​,​那么​下​一个​节点​为​右子​树​的​最小​节点​ */
    {
        __x = __x->_M_right;
        while ( __x->_M_left != 0 )
            __x = __x->_M_left;
    }else  {                        
        /* ​不​存在​右子​树​,​那么​分为​两种​情况​：​自底​往​上​搜索​,​当前​节点​为父​节点​的​左​孩子​的​时候​,​父​节点​就是​后继​节点​； */
/* ​第二种​情况​:_x​为​header​节点​了​,​那么​_x​就是​最后​的​后继​节点​. ​简言之​_x​为​最小​节点​且​往​上​回溯​,​一直​为父​节点​的​右​孩子​,​直到​_x​变为​父​节点​,_y​为​其右​孩子​ */
        _Rb_tree_node_base *__y = __x->_M_parent;
        while ( __x == __y->_M_right )
        {
            __x = __y;
            __y = __y->_M_parent;
        }
        if ( __x->_M_right != __y )
            __x = __y;
    }
    return (__x);
}
Overloading the -- operator:

_Self&
operator--() _GLIBCXX_NOEXCEPT
{
    _M_node = _Rb_tree_decrement(_M_node);
    return *this;
}
Similarly, _Rb_tree_decrement is backed by local_Rb_tree_decrement, implemented as follows:

static _Rb_tree_node_base *
local_Rb_tree_decrement( _Rb_tree_node_base * __x )
throw ()
{
/* header​节点​ */
    if ( __x->_M_color ==
         _S_red
         && __x
         ->_M_parent->_M_parent == __x )
        __x = __x->_M_right;
    else if ( __x->_M_left != 0 ) /* ​左​节点​不为​空​,​返回​左子​树中​最大​的​节点​ */
    {
        _Rb_tree_node_base *__y = __x->_M_left;
        while ( __y->_M_right != 0 )
            __y = __y->_M_right;
        __x = __y;
    }else  {
/* ​自​底向上​找到​当前​节点​为​其父​节点​的​右​孩子​,​那么​父​节点​就是​前驱​节点​ */
        _Rb_tree_node_base *__y = __x->_M_parent;
        while ( __x == __y->_M_left )
        {
            __x = __y;
            __y = __y->_M_parent;
        }
        __x = __y;
    }
    return
        (__x);
}

Overloading the == and != operators: just compare whether the node pointers are equal.

bool
operator==(const _Self& __x) const _GLIBCXX_NOEXCEPT
{ return _M_node == __x._M_node; }

bool
operator!=(const _Self& __x) const _GLIBCXX_NOEXCEPT
{ return _M_node != __x._M_node; }

Another important function, counting black nodes:

unsigned int
_Rb_tree_black_count(const _Rb_tree_node_base *__node,
                     const _Rb_tree_node_base *__root) throw() {
    if (__node == 0)
        return 0;
    unsigned int __sum = 0;
    do {
        if (__node->_M_color == _S_black)
            ++__sum;
        if (__node == __root)
            break;
        __node = __node->_M_parent;
    } while (1);
    return __sum;
}
Later we will explain the most important operation, insertion.

docs.title: 4.Red-black tree operations
docs.text:
Quite importantly, inside, a pointer is declared using the node base class. There is also a _Rb_tree_impl for the red-black tree's initialization and memory-management operations. It also contains two kinds of iterators, one rbtree and the other reverse, which shows that rbegin and rend operations are supported. 

template<typename _Key, typename _Val, typename _KeyOfValue,
           typename _Compare, typename _Alloc = allocator<_Val> >
class _Rb_tree
{

protected:
    typedef _Rb_tree_node_base*         _Base_ptr;

 template<typename _Key_compare, 
    bool _Is_pod_comparator = __is_pod(_Key_compare)>
    struct _Rb_tree_impl : public _Node_allocator
    {
      _Key_compare      _M_key_compare;
      _Rb_tree_node_base    _M_header;
      size_type         _M_node_count; // Keeps track of size of tree.

      _Rb_tree_impl()
      : _Node_allocator(), _M_key_compare(), _M_header(),
        _M_node_count(0)
      { _M_initialize(); }

      _Rb_tree_impl(const _Key_compare& __comp, const _Node_allocator& __a)
      : _Node_allocator(__a), _M_key_compare(__comp), _M_header(),
        _M_node_count(0)
      { _M_initialize(); }

    private:
      void
      _M_initialize()
      {
        this->_M_header._M_color = _S_red;
        this->_M_header._M_parent = 0;
        this->_M_header._M_left = &this->_M_header;
        this->_M_header._M_right = &this->_M_header;
      }  

    };
public: 
    typedef _Rb_tree_iterator<value_type>       iterator;
    typedef std::reverse_iterator<iterator>     reverse_iterator; 
private:
_Rb_tree_impl<_Compare> _M_impl;
};

Getting the red-black tree's root, leftmost, and rightmost nodes

Back to the figure from the beginning: .

// ​图中​100 ​节点​
 _Base_ptr&
_M_root() _GLIBCXX_NOEXCEPT
{ return this->_M_impl._M_header._M_parent; }

// ​图中​most left​标记​
_Base_ptr&
_M_leftmost() _GLIBCXX_NOEXCEPT
{ return this->_M_impl._M_header._M_left; }


// ​图中​most right​标记​
 _Base_ptr&
_M_rightmost() _GLIBCXX_NOEXCEPT
{ return this->_M_impl._M_header._M_right; }
 _Link_type

 // ​图中​begin()​标记​
_M_begin() _GLIBCXX_NOEXCEPT
{ return static_cast<_Link_type>(this->_M_impl._M_header._M_parent); }

// ​图中​end()​标记​
_Link_type
_M_end() _GLIBCXX_NOEXCEPT
{ return reinterpret_cast<_Link_type>(&this->_M_impl._M_header); }
Looking at the code again — isn't everything crystal clear!

docs.title: 5.1 The rotation process
docs.text:
A left rotation sets the node's right child as its parent, and the node becomes the left child of that former right child.

Just compare the figure in the source code with the code directly.

In the tree.cc source the implementing functions are local_Rb_tree_rotate_left and local_Rb_tree_rotate_right. Below we dissect the source into easier-to-understand code; see the comments for details. You will notice the function and variable names differ from the source — that is because the code below was my own implementation at the time, but it does not hinder reading the source, so it is used directly for comparison.

/**
* ​当前​节点​的​左​旋转​过程​
* ​将​该​节点​的​右​节点​设置​为​它​的​父​节点​，​该​节点​将​变成​刚才​右​节点​的​左​孩子​
* @param _x
*/
//    _x                      _y
//  /   \     ​左​旋转​         /  \
// T1   _y   --------->   _x    T3
//     / \              /   \
//    T2 T3            T1   T2
void leftRotate(Node *_x) {
    // step1 ​处理​_x​的​右​孩子​
    // ​右​节点​变为​_x​节点​的​父亲​节点​,​先​保存​一下​右​节点​
    Node *_y = _x->right;
    // T2​变为​node​的​右​节点​
    _x->right = _y->left;
    if (NULL != _y->left)
        _y->left->parent = _x;

    // step2 ​处理​_y​与​父亲​节点​关系​
    _y->parent = _x->parent;      // ​原来​_x​的​父亲​变为​_y​的​父亲​
    // ​说明​原来​_x​为​root​节点​,​此时​需要​将​_y​设为​新​root​节点​
    // ​或者​判断​NULL == _y->parent
    if (_x == root)
        root = _y;
    else if (_x == _x->parent->left)    // ​原​_x​的​父​节点​的​左​孩子​连接​新​节点​_y
        _x->parent->left = _y;
    else // ​原​_x​的​父​节点​的​右​孩子​连接​新​节点​_y
        _x->parent->right = _y;

    // step3 ​处理​_x​与​_y​关系​
    _y->left = _x;      // _y​的​左​孩子​为​_x
    _x->parent = _y;    // _x​的​父亲​是​_y
}

Similarly, the right rotation is as follows: 

//        _x                      _y
//      /   \     ​右​旋转​         /  \
//     _y    T2 ------------->  T0  _x
//    /  \                         /  \
//   T0  T1                       T1  T2
void rightRotate(Node *_x) {
    // step1 ​处理​_x​的​左​孩子​
    // ​左​节点​变为​_x​节点​的​父亲​节点​,​先​保存​一下​左​节点​
    Node *_y = _x->left;
    // T1​变为​_x​的​左​孩子​
    _x->left = _y->right;
    if (NULL != _y->right)
        _y->right->parent = _x;

    // step2 ​处理​_y​与​父​节点​之间​的​关系​
    // ​或者​判断​_x->parent==NULL
    if (_x == root)
        root = _y;
    else if (_x == _x->parent->right)
        _x->parent->right = _y;
    else
        _x->parent->left = _y;

    // step3 ​处理​_x​与​_y​关系​
    _y->right = _x;     // _y​的​右​孩子​为​_x
    _x->parent = _y;    // _x​的​父亲​是​_y
}

case 1.1: The parent is red and its uncle is also red; then set the parent and uncle to black, and the grandparent to red.

case 1.2 If there is no uncle, or the uncle is black, it splits into the following two:

Situation 1.2.1: x's uncle y is black and x is a right child

Situation 1.2.2: x's uncle y is black and x is a left child

Corresponding to this in the source code: 

_Rb_tree_node_base *const __y = __xpp->_M_right;    // ​得到​叔叔​节点​
if (__y && __y->_M_color == _S_red)     // case1: ​叔叔​节点​存在​，​且​为​红色​
{
    /**
        * ​解决办法​是​：​颜色​翻转​，​父亲​与​叔叔​的​颜色​都​变为​黑色​,​祖父​节点​变为​红色​,​然后​当前​节点​设​为​祖父​，​依次​网上​来​判断​是否​破坏​了​红​黑树​性质​
        */
    __x->_M_parent->_M_color = _S_black;    // ​将​其父​节点​改为​黑色​
    __y->_M_color = _S_black;               // ​将​其​叔叔​节点​改为​黑色​
    __xpp->_M_color = _S_red;               // ​将​其​祖父​节点​改为​红色​
    __x = __xpp;                            // ​修改​_x,​往​上​回溯​
} else {        // ​无​叔叔​或者​叔叔​为​黑色​
    if (__x == __x->_M_parent->_M_right) {          // ​当前​节点​为​父亲​节点​的​右​孩子​
        __x = __x->_M_parent;
        local_Rb_tree_rotate_left(__x, __root);     // ​以父​节点​进行​左​旋转​
    }
    // ​旋转​之后​,​节点​x​变成​其父​节点​的​左​孩子​
    __x->_M_parent->_M_color = _S_black;            // ​将​其​父亲​节点​改为​黑色​
    __xpp->_M_color = _S_red;                       // ​将​其​祖父​节点​改为​红色​
    local_Rb_tree_rotate_right(__xpp, __root);      // ​以​祖父​节点​右​旋转​
}

The other one is the symmetric process of the above:

case 2.1: The parent is red and its uncle is also red; then set the parent and uncle to black, and the grandparent to red.

case 2.2 If there is no uncle, or the uncle is black

Situation 2.2.1: x's uncle y is black and x is a left child

_Rb_tree_node_base *const __y = __xpp->_M_left; // ​保存​叔叔​节点​
if (__y && __y->_M_color == _S_red) {       // ​叔叔​节点​存在​且​为​红色​
    __x->_M_parent->_M_color = _S_black;    // ​父亲​节点​改为​黑色​
    __y->_M_color = _S_black;               // ​祖父​节点​改为​红色​
    __xpp->_M_color = _S_red;
    __x = __xpp;
} else {        // ​若​无​叔叔​节点​或者​其​叔叔​节点​为​黑色​
    if (__x == __x->_M_parent->_M_left) {   // ​当前​节点​为​父亲​节点​的​左​孩子​
        __x = __x->_M_parent;
        local_Rb_tree_rotate_right(__x, __root);    // ​以父​节点​右​旋转​
    }
    __x->_M_parent->_M_color = _S_black;        // ​父​节点​置​为​黑色​
    __xpp->_M_color = _S_red;                   // ​祖父​节点​置​为​红色​
    local_Rb_tree_rotate_left(__xpp, __root);   // ​左​旋转​
}

Full dissection of _Rb_tree_insert_and_rebalance:

void
_Rb_tree_insert_and_rebalance(const bool __insert_left,
                              _Rb_tree_node_base *__x,
                              _Rb_tree_node_base *__p,
                              _Rb_tree_node_base &__header) throw() {
    _Rb_tree_node_base * &__root = __header._M_parent;

    // Initialize fields in new node to insert.
    __x->_M_parent = __p;
    __x->_M_left = 0;
    __x->_M_right = 0;
    __x->_M_color = _S_red;

    // ​处理​__header​部分​
    // Insert.
    // Make new node child of parent and maintain root, leftmost and
    // rightmost nodes.
    // N.B. First node is always inserted left.
    if (__insert_left) {
        __p->_M_left = __x; // also makes leftmost = __x when __p == &__header

        if (__p == &__header) {
            __header._M_parent = __x;
            __header._M_right = __x;
        } else if (__p == __header._M_left)
            __header._M_left = __x; // maintain leftmost pointing to min node
    } else {
        __p->_M_right = __x;

        if (__p == __header._M_right)
            __header._M_right = __x; // maintain rightmost pointing to max node
    }

 // Rebalance.
    while (__x != __root
           && __x->_M_parent->_M_color == _S_red)   // ​若​新​插入​节点​不是​为​RB-Tree​的​根​节点​，​且​其父​节点​color​属性​也​是​红色​,​即​违反​了​性质​4.
    {
        _Rb_tree_node_base *const __xpp = __x->_M_parent->_M_parent;        // ​祖父​节点​

        if (__x->_M_parent == __xpp->_M_left)   // ​父亲​是​祖父​节点​的​左​孩子​
        {
            _Rb_tree_node_base *const __y = __xpp->_M_right;    // ​得到​叔叔​节点​
            if (__y && __y->_M_color == _S_red)     // case1: ​叔叔​节点​存在​，​且​为​红色​
            {
                /**
                 * ​解决办法​是​：​颜色​翻转​，​父亲​与​叔叔​的​颜色​都​变为​黑色​,​祖父​节点​变为​红色​,​然后​当前​节点​设​为​祖父​，​依次​网上​来​判断​是否​破坏​了​红​黑树​性质​
                 */
                __x->_M_parent->_M_color = _S_black;    // ​将​其父​节点​改为​黑色​
                __y->_M_color = _S_black;               // ​将​其​叔叔​节点​改为​黑色​
                __xpp->_M_color = _S_red;               // ​将​其​祖父​节点​改为​红色​
                __x = __xpp;                            // ​修改​_x,​往​上​回溯​
            } else {        // ​无​叔叔​或者​叔叔​为​黑色​
                if (__x == __x->_M_parent->_M_right) {          // ​当前​节点​为​父亲​节点​的​右​孩子​
                    __x = __x->_M_parent;
                    local_Rb_tree_rotate_left(__x, __root);     // ​以父​节点​进行​左​旋转​
                }
                // ​旋转​之后​,​节点​x​变成​其父​节点​的​左​孩子​
                __x->_M_parent->_M_color = _S_black;            // ​将​其​父亲​节点​改为​黑色​
                __xpp->_M_color = _S_red;                       // ​将​其​祖父​节点​改为​红色​
                local_Rb_tree_rotate_right(__xpp, __root);      // ​以​祖父​节点​右​旋转​
            }
        } else {        // ​父亲​是​祖父​节点​的​右​孩子​
            _Rb_tree_node_base *const __y = __xpp->_M_left; // ​保存​叔叔​节点​
            if (__y && __y->_M_color == _S_red) {       // ​叔叔​节点​存在​且​为​红色​
                __x->_M_parent->_M_color = _S_black;    // ​父亲​节点​改为​黑色​
                __y->_M_color = _S_black;               // ​祖父​节点​改为​红色​
                __xpp->_M_color = _S_red;
                __x = __xpp;
            } else {        // ​若​无​叔叔​节点​或者​其​叔叔​节点​为​黑色​
                if (__x == __x->_M_parent->_M_left) {   // ​当前​节点​为​父亲​节点​的​左​孩子​
                    __x = __x->_M_parent;
                    local_Rb_tree_rotate_right(__x, __root);    // ​以父​节点​右​旋转​
                }
                __x->_M_parent->_M_color = _S_black;        // ​父​节点​置​为​黑色​
                __xpp->_M_color = _S_red;                   // ​祖父​节点​置​为​红色​
                local_Rb_tree_rotate_left(__xpp, __root);   // ​左​旋转​
            }
        }
    }
    //​若​新​插入​节点​为根​节点​,​则​违反​性质​2
    //​只​需​将​其​重新​赋值​为​黑色​即可​
    __root->_M_color = _S_black;
}

docs.title: 5.2 Insertion summary
docs.text:
From the insertion process and source analysis above, we derive the following three cases: Let P stand for the parent node, N for the newly inserted node, U for the uncle, and G for the grandparent.

case 1: U is red, and P and N are also red; then, by changing colors and adjusting recursively bottom-up, next time N becomes G, and we just keep judging upward. If the root happens to get colored red, the algorithm can force root back to black at the very end.

case 2: U is black; consider whether N is P's left or right child.

case2.1 If it is a right child, first do a left rotation, then move on to the next case.

case2.2 May have evolved from the case above, but not necessarily! The strategy: rotate right and change colors.

From the source analysis above we learn that red-black tree insertion is a mirror transformation; the other case is exactly the reverse.

The deletion operation is rather complex, so it is not analyzed here for now; to be added later...

docs.title: STL set and multiset
docs.text:
set/multiset use rb_tree as their underlying structure, and therefore have the characteristic of automatic element sorting. Sorting is based on the key, and for set/multiset elements the value and the key are one and the same: the value is the key.

We cannot use set/multiset iterators to change element values (because the key has its strict ordering rules). The iterators of set/multiset are the const-iterators of the underlying RB tree, precisely to forbid users from assigning to elements.

The key of a set element must be unique, so its insert uses the rb_tree's _M_insert_unique(), while the key of a multiset element may repeat, so its insert uses the rb_tree's _M_insert_equal().

docs.title: 1.set
docs.text:
The source code of set is fairly simple, so let's start from the following questions.

First question: the key is the value, and the value is also the key.

The concrete code will appear in the second question; here we give the internal logic after the code we usually write. We see there is a red-black tree inside, and in the red-black tree's definition the key and the value are the same, which answers this question. (In the source code the typedefs all come from the key.)

template<typename _Key, typename _Compare = std::less<_Key>,
    typename _Alloc = std::allocator<_Key> >
class set
{
    // concept requirements
    typedef typename _Alloc::value_type                   _Alloc_value_type;

public:
    // typedefs:
    //@{
    /// Public typedefs.
    typedef _Key     key_type;
    typedef _Key     value_type; // value​也​是​key
    typedef _Compare key_compare;
    typedef _Compare value_compare;
    typedef _Alloc   allocator_type;
    //@}

private:

    typedef _Rb_tree<key_type, value_type, _Identity<value_type>,
            key_compare, _Key_alloc_type> _Rep_type;
    _Rep_type _M_t;  // Red-black tree representing set.
};

Second question: element values cannot be changed via iterators.

For not being able to change element values via iterators, we look at the iterators later and find that they all use const_iterator, so the second question is answered as well.

template<typename _Key, typename _Compare = std::less<_Key>,
    typename _Alloc = std::allocator<_Key> >
class set
{
private:

    typedef _Rb_tree<key_type, value_type, _Identity<value_type>,
            key_compare, _Key_alloc_type> _Rep_type;
    _Rep_type _M_t;  // Red-black tree representing set.

public:
    typedef typename _Rep_type::const_iterator            iterator;
    typedef typename _Rep_type::const_iterator            const_iterator;
    typedef typename _Rep_type::const_reverse_iterator    reverse_iterator;
    typedef typename _Rep_type::const_reverse_iterator const_reverse_iterator;
};

The analysis above reminds us of queue, priority_queue, and stack: they all use an underlying container, which is why they are called container adaptors. set likewise uses an underlying container, so it too can be called a container adapter.

Third question: insertion requires a unique key.

What gets called underneath is _M_insert_unique. 

template<typename _InputIterator>
set(_InputIterator __first, _InputIterator __last)
: _M_t()
{ _M_t._M_insert_unique(__first, __last); }

Let's take a quick look at this function's implementation: Below, _M_get_insert_unique_pos returns a pair; if the inserted key is the same, the pair's second is 0, so whether the key duplicates can be judged from whether it is 0. In the check in the code below, when second is not 0 — that is, not a duplicate — it can be inserted directly, in which case a pair with second true is constructed directly; otherwise a pair with second false is constructed.

template<typename _Key, typename _Val, typename _KeyOfValue,
     typename _Compare, typename _Alloc>
#if __cplusplus >= 201103L
template<typename _Arg>
#endif
pair<typename _Rb_tree<_Key, _Val, _KeyOfValue,
               _Compare, _Alloc>::iterator, bool>
_Rb_tree<_Key, _Val, _KeyOfValue, _Compare, _Alloc>::
_M_insert_unique( _Arg && __v )

{
    typedef pair<iterator, bool> _Res;
    pair<_Base_ptr, _Base_ptr> __res
        = _M_get_insert_unique_pos( _KeyOfValue() ( __v ) );

    if ( __res.second )
        return(_Res( _M_insert_( __res.first, __res.second,
                     _GLIBCXX_FORWARD( _Arg, __v ) ),
                 true ) );

    return(_Res( iterator( static_cast<_Link_type>(__res.first) ), false ) );
}

Let's also look at the function mentioned above: 

template<typename _Key, typename _Val, typename _KeyOfValue,typename _Compare, typename _Alloc>
pair<typename _Rb_tree<_Key, _Val, _KeyOfValue,
_Compare, _Alloc>::_Base_ptr,typename _Rb_tree<_Key, _Val, _KeyOfValue,Compare, _Alloc>::_Base_ptr>
_Rb_tree<_Key, _Val, _KeyOfValue, _Compare, _Alloc>::
_M_get_insert_unique_pos(const key_type& __k)
{
    // typedef pair
    typedef pair<_Base_ptr, _Base_ptr> _Res;
    // _x​表示​当前​节点​,_y​表示​_x​的​父​节点​
    _Link_type __x = _M_begin();
    _Link_type __y = _M_end();
    bool __comp = true;

    // ​寻找​插入​点​
    while (__x != 0)
    {
        __y = __x;
        // __k<__x​是否​为​true
        __comp = _M_impl._M_key_compare(__k, _S_key(__x));
        // __k<__x​就​往​左​孩子​查找​，​否则​右​孩子​查找​
        __x = __comp ? _S_left(__x) : _S_right(__x);
    }
    iterator __j = iterator(__y);
    // __k<__y，​往​__y​的​左​孩子​插入​节点​即可​，​不是​做​插入​，​是​找到​位置​即可​。
    if (__comp)
    {
        // ​特殊​位置​
        if (__j == begin())
        return _Res(__x, __y);
        else
        --__j;  // ​左​孩子​ ​这里​调用​了​--​操作符​
    }
    // __j<__k，​返回​当前​节​(__x=0)​点​与​父​节点​
    if (_M_impl._M_key_compare(_S_key(__j._M_node), __k))
        return _Res(__x, __y);
    // _j>=__k,​插入​失败​
    return _Res(__j._M_node, 0);
}

The use of pair above gave me an insight — so it can be used like this! Let's learn it: 

cout<<"flag: "<<itree._M_insert_unique(5).second<<endl;  // ​学习​返回值​
typedef pair<int ,bool> _Res;    // ​也​来​用​一下​typedef​后​的​pair
cout<<_Res(1,true).first<<endl;  // ​直接​包裹​
_Res r=make_pair(2,false);    // ​定义新​对象​
cout<<r.first<<endl;   // ​输出​结果​

docs.title: 2.multiset
docs.text:
Similarly, multiset is defined basically like set; the difference is that its insertion uses another function, which is what enables it to accomplish inserting duplicate keys!

 template<typename _InputIterator>
multiset(_InputIterator __first, _InputIterator __last)
: _M_t()
{ _M_t._M_insert_equal(__first, __last); }
Next let's analyze _M_insert_equal:

typename _Rb_tree<_Key, _Val, _KeyOfValue, _Compare, _Alloc>::iterator
_Rb_tree<_Key, _Val, _KeyOfValue, _Compare, _Alloc>::
_M_insert_equal(_Arg&& __v)
{
    pair<_Base_ptr, _Base_ptr> __res = _M_get_insert_equal_pos(_KeyOfValue()(__v));
    return _M_insert_(__res.first, __res.second, _GLIBCXX_FORWARD(_Arg, __v));
}

We continue tracing the _M_get_insert_equal_pos function above:

template<typename _Key, typename _Val, typename _KeyOfValue,
typename _Compare, typename _Alloc>
pair<typename _Rb_tree<_Key, _Val, _KeyOfValue,
_Compare, _Alloc>::_Base_ptr,
typename _Rb_tree<_Key, _Val, _KeyOfValue,
_Compare, _Alloc>::_Base_ptr>
_Rb_tree<_Key, _Val, _KeyOfValue, _Compare, _Alloc>::
_M_get_insert_equal_pos(const key_type& __k)
{
    typedef pair<_Base_ptr, _Base_ptr> _Res;
    _Link_type __x = _M_begin();
    _Link_type __y = _M_end();
    while (__x != 0)
    {
        __y = __x;
        __x = _M_impl._M_key_compare(__k, _S_key(__x)) ?
            _S_left(__x) : _S_right(__x);
    }
    return _Res(__x, __y);
}
Comparing these functions of multiset and set, we find a striking difference in the returned pair: the previous set needed to return whether the insertion ultimately succeeded, because keys cannot repeat, whereas multiset does not need to return insertion success, so its pair contains no bool type — it directly returns the pair formed from the insertion point. Therefore, compared with before, no matter how many keys you have or how they repeat, they can all be inserted.

docs.title: STL iterator invalidation
docs.text:
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/6438086/iterator-invalidation-rules-for-c-containers

Insertion Sequential containers

  • vector: all iterators and references before the insertion point are unaffected, unless the new container size exceeds the previous capacity (in which case all iterators and references are invalidated) [23.3.6.5/1]
  • deque: all iterators and references are invalidated, unless the inserted element is at either end of the deque (front or back) (in which case all iterators are invalidated, but references to elements are unaffected) [23.3.3.4/1]
  • list: all iterators and references remain unaffected [23.3.5.4/1]
  • forward_list: all iterators and references remain unaffected (applies to insert_after) [23.3.4.5/1]
  • array: (not applicable)

Associative containers

  • [multi]{set,map}: all iterators and references remain unaffected [23.2.4/9]

Unordered associative containers

  • unordered_[multi]{set,map}: when a rehash happens, all iterators are invalidated, but references are unaffected [23.2.⅝]. No rehash occurs if the insertion does not cause the container's size to exceed z * B, where z is the maximum load factor and B is the current number of buckets [23.2.5/14]

Container adaptors

  • stack: inherited from the underlying container
  • queue: inherited from the underlying container
  • priority_queue: inherited from the underlying container

Erasure Sequential containers

  • vector: every iterator and reference at or after the point of erasure is invalidated [23.3.6.5/3]
  • deque: erasing the last element invalidates only iterators and references to the erased element and the past-the-end iterator; erasing the first element invalidates only iterators and references to the erased element; erasing any other element invalidates all iterators and references (including the past-the-end iterator) [23.3.3.4/4]
  • list: only iterators and references to the erased element are invalidated [23.3.5.4/3]
  • forward_list: only iterators and references to the erased element are invalidated (applies to erase_after) [23.3.4.5/1]
  • array: (not applicable)

Associative containers

  • [multi]{set,map}: only iterators and references to the erased element are invalidated [23.2.4/9]

Unordered associative containers

  • unordered_[multi]{set,map}: only iterators and references to the erased element are invalidated [23.2.5/13]

Container adaptors

  • stack: inherited from the underlying container
  • queue: inherited from the underlying container
  • priority_queue: inherited from the underlying container

Resizing - vector: same as insertion/erasure [23.3.6.5/12] - deque: same as insertion/erasure [23.3.3.3/3] - list: same as insertion/erasure [23.3.5.3/1] - forward_list: same as insertion/erasure [23.3.4.5/25] - array: (not applicable)

Note 1 Unless expressly stated otherwise (either explicitly or by defining a function in terms of other functions), calling a container member function or passing a container as an argument to a library function shall not invalidate iterators to (or change the value of) objects within that container. [23.2.1/11]

Note 2 No swap() function invalidates any references, pointers, or iterators referring to the elements of the containers being swapped. [Note: the end() iterator does not refer to any element, so it may be invalidated. — end note] [23.2.1/10]

Note 3 Except for the swap() caveat above, it is not clear whether the "end" iterators are subject to the rules for each container above; in any case, you should assume that they are.

Note 4 vector and all unordered associative containers support reserve(n), which guarantees that no automatic resizing will occur at least until the container size grows to n. Be careful with unordered associative containers, because future proposals will allow setting a minimum load factor, which would allow a rehash to happen on insertion after enough erasures shrink the container below that minimum; so after erasures this guarantee should be considered potentially invalid.

docs.title: STL traits type extraction | C++​那些​事
docs.text: Last updated：2026-10-13

docs.title: 0.Introduction
docs.text:
In STL programming, containers and algorithms are designed independently, that is, data structures and algorithms are designed separately; the bridge connecting containers and algorithms is the iterator, and iterators make this independent design possible. As shown in the figure below:

The figure above shows that the goal of the STL is to separate data from algorithms, design each of them independently, and then glue the two back together through something called an iterator.

In design patterns, iterator is described as: a way to access each element of a container sequentially without exposing the container's internal representation. And type extraction (traits) technology exists precisely to solve problems related to iterators.

To apply generic algorithms (find, count, find_if) to a container, the most important thing is to provide the algorithm with a tool for accessing the container's elements, and the iterator plays this important role.

Inside an algorithm we may need to define simple intermediate variables or set the type of the algorithm's return variable; at that point we need to know what the type of the element the iterator points to is. But since there is no typeof-like function for deducing types, we cannot obtain it directly — so what can be done? This article explains it in detail.

An iterator is a kind of smart pointer, and therefore it has all the characteristics of an ordinary pointer — you can apply * and -> operations to it. However, when traversing a container, it is unavoidable to know something about the container's internals, so it is simply better to leave the development of iterators to the container's designers. That way, all implementation details are encapsulated and hidden from users — which is exactly why every STL container provides its own dedicated iterators.

And Traits is in bits/stl_iterator_base_types.h:

template<class _Tp>
struct iterator_traits<_Tp*>
{
    typedef ptrdiff_t difference_type;
    typedef typename _Tp::value_type value_type;
    typedef typename _Tp::pointer pointer;
    typedef typename _Tp::reference reference;
    typedef typename _Tp::iterator_category iterator_category;
};

Looks totally baffling, right? No worries — after reading this section you'll have gotten started with the STL, haha~

docs.title: 1.template parameter deduction
docs.text:
First, when using iterators in algorithms, you will very likely need their associated types (the type of what the iterator points to). Suppose the algorithm needs to declare a variable whose type is "the type of the object the iterator points to" — what should we do?

The solution: use function template's parameter deduction mechanism.

For example:

If T is a pointer to some object, what do we do when func needs the type of the object the pointer points to? This one is fairly easy; the template's parameter deduction mechanism can do the job,

template <class I>
inline
void func(I iter) {
    func_impl(iter, *iter); // ​传入​iter​和​iter​所指​的​值​，class​自动​推导​
}

Through the template's deduction mechanism, we effortlessly obtain the type of the object the pointer points to.

template <class I, class T>
void func_impl(I iter, T t) {
        T tmp; // ​这里​就是​迭代​器​所指​物​的​类别​
        // ... ​功能​实现​
}

int main() {
    int i;
    func(&i);
}

However, what the function's "template parameter deduction mechanism" deduces are only parameters; it cannot deduce the function's return type. If the function's return type needs to be deduced, it is powerless. Therefore, we introduce the following method.

docs.title: 2.Declaring nested types
docs.text:
The type of the object an iterator points to is called the iterator's value type.

Although in func_impl we can use T as the function's return value, the problem is that what users need to call is func.

template <class I, class T>
T func_impl(I iter, T t) {
        T tmp; // ​这里​就是​迭代​器​所指​物​的​类别​
        // ... ​功能​实现​
}
template <class T>
(*T) func(T t) { // !!!Wrong code
    return func_impl(t, *t); // forward the task to func_impl
}
int main() {
    int i  =10;
    cout<<func(&i)<<endl; // !!! Can’t pass compile
}

If you try to compile the code above, compilation fails!

This problem is not hard to solve either: declaring a nested type seems like a good idea, so that we can obtain it directly. Just make an iterator, and when defining it give an alias to the type of the object it points to — done, like this:

template <class T>
struct MyIter {
    typedef T value_type; // ​内嵌​型别​声明​
    T* ptr;
    MyIter(T* p = 0) : ptr(p) {}
    T& operator*() const { return *ptr; }
};

template <class I>
typename I::value_type
func(I ite) {
    std::cout << "class version" << std::endl;
    return *ite;
}
int main() {
    // ...
    MyIter<int> ite(new int(8));
    cout << func(ite);  // ​输出​8
}

A very elegant solution; everything looks perfect. But in fact there is still a problem, because if func is a generic algorithm, it must absolutely also accept a native pointer as an iterator, yet clearly you cannot get the following code to compile:

int *p = new int(5);
cout<<func(p)<<endl; // error

Our func cannot support native pointers, which is clearly unacceptable. At this point, template partial specialization comes to the rescue.

docs.title: 3.The savior Traits
docs.text:
As mentioned earlier, if we use typename I::value_type directly, the algorithm cannot accept native pointers, because a native pointer simply has no nested type called value_type.

Therefore, we still need to add an intermediate layer to determine whether it is a native pointer — and note, this is exactly the beauty of the traits technique.

If we only use the approach above, i.e. the nested value_type, then for pointers without value_type we can only partially specialize — and it would be a partial specialization of the callable function func. If func had a million lines of code, this would cause enormous visual pollution.

(1) Function partial specialization

Function partial specialization:

template <class T>
struct MyIter {
    typedef T value_type; // ​内嵌​型别​声明​
    T* ptr;
    MyIter(T* p = 0) : ptr(p) {}
    T& operator*() const { return *ptr; }
};

template <class I>
typename I::value_type
func(I ite) {
    std::cout << "class version" << std::endl;
    return *ite;
}
template <class I>
I
func(I* ite) {
    std::cout << "pointer version" << std::endl;
    return *ite;
}
template <class I>
I func(const I* ite) {
    std::cout << "const pointer version" << std::endl;
    return *ite;
}
int main() {
    // ...
    MyIter<int> ite(new int(8));
    cout << func(ite)<<endl;
    int *p = new int(52);
    cout<<func(p)<<endl;
    const int k = 3;
    cout<<func(&k)<<endl;
}

Output:

class version
8
pointer version
52
const pointer version
3

(2) Adding an intermediate layer

What is Traits in the STL? Look at the figure below:

Using an intermediate layer iterator_traits fixes the form of func, eliminating a large amount of duplicated code; the only thing left to do is slightly specialize iterator_tartis so that it supports pointer and const pointer:)

#include <iostream>

template <class T>
struct MyIter {
    typedef T value_type; // ​内嵌​型别​声明​
    T* ptr;
    MyIter(T* p = 0) : ptr(p) {}
    T& operator*() const { return *ptr; }
};
// class type
template <class T>
struct iterator_traits {
    typedef typename T::value_type value_type;
};
// ​偏​特化​1
template <class T>
struct iterator_traits<T*> {
    typedef T value_type;
};
// ​偏​特化​2
template <class T>
struct iterator_traits<const T*> {
    typedef T value_type;
};

template <class I>
typename iterator_traits<I>::value_type
// ​首先​询问​iterator_traits<I>::value_type,​如果​传递​的​I​为​指针​,​则​进入​特化​版本​,iterator_traits​直接​回答​;​如果​传递​进来​的​I​为​class type,​就​去​询问​T::value_type.
func(I ite) {
    std::cout << "normal version" << std::endl;
    return *ite;
}
int main() {
    // ...
    MyIter<int> ite(new int(8));
    std::cout << func(ite)<<std::endl;
    int *p = new int(52);
    std::cout<<func(p)<<std::endl;
    const int k = 3;
    std::cout<<func(&k)<<std::endl;
}

The process above first asks iterator_traits<I>::value_type: if the passed-in I is a pointer, the specialized version is entered and iterator_traits answers directly with T; if the passed-in I is a class type, it goes on to ask T::value_type.

Put plainly: the algorithm (func) asks iterator_traits (me), but when iterator_traits (me) finds a pointer in hand, I answer on its behalf. If it is a class type, iterator_traits (me) keeps asking (him --- T::value_type).

Summary: by defining nested types, we gained a way to know the type of the element an iterator points to; through the traits technique, we unified the function template's definitions for native pointers and custom iterators. The main reason we use the traits technique is to resolve the code duplication caused by the differences between native pointers and custom iterators — this is exactly the beauty of the traits technique.

https://www.cnblogs.com/mangoyuan/p/6446046.html

docs.title: STL typename source code analysis | C++​那些​事
docs.text: Last updated：2026-10-13

docs.title: STL typename source code analysis
docs.text:
There are a few lines like the following in the underlying STL source code, with typedef used together with typename. They look quite complicated. What exactly do they mean? Let's dissect them together today!

template<typename _Iterator>
struct iterator_traits
{
  typedef typename _Iterator::iterator_category iterator_category;
  typedef typename _Iterator::value_type        value_type;
  typedef typename _Iterator::difference_type   difference_type;
  typedef typename _Iterator::pointer           pointer;
  typedef typename _Iterator::reference         reference;
};

docs.title: Common usage of typename
docs.text:
First, let's learn the common usage of typename:

template <typename T>
int compare(const T &a, const T &b)
{
    return a>b?a:b;
}

The above is just a sample program; to write a complete comparison, you would also need to consider specialized versions. You might think that replacing typename with class in the code above works just as well — right! So here comes the question: is there any difference between the two? After consulting C++ Primer, it turns out they are exactly the same.

docs.title: Class scope
docs.text:
When accessing names inside a class from outside the class, you can use the class scope operator. Calls of the form MyClass::name usually come in three kinds: static data members, static member functions, and nested types:

struct MyClass {
    static int A; //​静态​成员​
    static int B(){cout<<"B()"<<endl; return 100;} //​静态​函数​
    typedef int C;  //​嵌套​类型​
    struct A1 { //​嵌套​类型​
        static int s;
    };
};

When calling, you can call directly:

cout<<MyClass::A<<endl;
cout<<MyClass::B()<<endl;
MyClass:C c;
...

docs.title: A complete example
docs.text:
Let's return to a typename example:

template <class T>
void foo() {
    T::iterator * iter;
    // ...
}

What is the purpose of this code? Most people's first reaction might be: the author wants to define a pointer iter whose type is the iterator contained in the class scope T. There could be a structure containing an iterator type like this:

struct MyIterator {
    struct iterator {

    };
};

Called as follows:

foo<MyIterator>();

This way, the iter line is clear: it is a pointer of type MyIterator::iterator. That is our guess — but is it what actually happens?

But what about something like T::iterator? T is a type parameter in a template; which type it is will only be known when the template is instantiated, let alone the iterator inside it. From the introduction to class scope above, we know that T::iterator could in fact be any of the following three kinds:

  • static data member
  • static member function
  • nested type

The ContainsAType::iterator in the previous example is a nested type, which is perfectly fine. But what if it is a static data member? What if the type used to instantiate the foo template function looks like this:

struct MyIterator {
    static int iterator;
};

Then T::iterator * iter; is instantiated by the compiler as MyIterator::iterator * iter; — what is this? The leading part is a static member variable rather than a type, so this becomes a multiplication expression, except that iter is not defined here, and the compiler reports an error:

error: no type named ‘iterator’ in ‘struct MyIterator’

docs.title: typename
docs.text:
For a name used inside a template definition that depends on a template parameter, the compiler will treat the name as a type only if that type name exists among the instantiation arguments, or if the name is preceded by the typename keyword. Apart from these two cases, it will never be treated as a type.

Therefore, if you want to tell the compiler directly that T::iterator is a type and not a variable, you only need to qualify it with typename:

template <class T>
void foo() {
    typename T::iterator * iter;
}

This way the compiler can determine that T::iterator is a type without having to wait until instantiation, thereby eliminating the ambiguity mentioned earlier.

docs.title: Dissecting the source code
docs.text:
Back to the STL source code

template<typename _Iterator>
struct iterator_traits
{
  typedef typename _Iterator::iterator_category iterator_category;
  typedef typename _Iterator::value_type        value_type;
  typedef typename _Iterator::difference_type   difference_type;
  typedef typename _Iterator::pointer           pointer;
  typedef typename _Iterator::reference         reference;
};

Seeing the above, it becomes clear at once: it is nothing more than using typename to tell the compiler that _Iterator::iterator_category is a type, then using typedef to rename it — the rest is similar!

docs.title: STL unordered_map source code analysis | C++​那些​事
docs.text: Last updated：2026-10-13

docs.title: 0.Introduction
docs.text:
We learned about hashtable earlier; this section covers its container adaptor: unordered_map.

So the unordered map's underlying container is a hashtable.

The source of unordered_map and unordered_multimap lives in the file unordered_map.h.

docs.title: 1.The essential difference between unordered_map and unordered_multimap
docs.text:
First, a look at the unordered_map source:

template<class _Key, class _Tp,
class _Hash = hash<_Key>,
class _Pred = std::equal_to<_Key>,
class _Alloc = std::allocator<std::pair<const _Key, _Tp> > >
class unordered_map
{
    typedef __umap_hashtable<_Key, _Tp, _Hash, _Pred, _Alloc>  _Hashtable;
    _Hashtable _M_h;
};

Go look at the declaration of the underlying container __umap_hashtable:

template<bool _Cache>
using __umap_traits = __detail::_Hashtable_traits<_Cache, false, true>;

template<typename _Key,
    typename _Tp,
    typename _Hash = hash<_Key>,
    typename _Pred = std::equal_to<_Key>,
    typename _Alloc = std::allocator<std::pair<const _Key, _Tp> >,
    typename _Tr = __umap_traits<__cache_default<_Key, _Hash>::value>>
using __umap_hashtable = _Hashtable<_Key, std::pair<const _Key, _Tp>,
_Alloc, __detail::_Select1st,
_Pred, _Hash,
__detail::_Mod_range_hashing,
__detail::_Default_ranged_hash,
__detail::_Prime_rehash_policy, _Tr>;
We can draw the following conclusion: the hashtable's template parameters: 
template<typename _Key, typename _Value, typename _Alloc,
typename _ExtractKey, typename _Equal,
typename _H1, typename _H2, typename _Hash,
typename _RehashPolicy, typename _Traits>
By default, unordered_map uses: - H1 is hash - H2 is _Mod_range_hashing - _Hash is _Default_ranged_hash - _RehashPolicy is _Prime_rehash_policy - _Traits is _Tr The final _Tr is very important, because it is precisely due to this parameter that unordered_multimap exists. See the concrete analysis below:

_Tr is as follows:

typename _Tr = __umap_traits<__cache_default<_Key, _Hash>::value>>
_Tr uses __umap_traits; let's keep going: 
template<bool _Cache>
using __umap_traits = __detail::_Hashtable_traits<_Cache, false, true>;
Comparing the two above, we find that inside __umap_traits there is a string of __cache_default. The template parameter is of bool type, so we can print whether it is false or true; by actual testing it is false, meaning the hash code is not cached.

template<typename _Tp, typename _Hash>
using __cache_default
=  __not_<__and_<__is_fast_hash<_Hash>,
__detail::__is_noexcept_hash<_Tp, _Hash>>>;
Continuing with __umap_traits, which actually calls _Hashtable_traits; we keep going:

template<bool _Cache_hash_code, bool _Constant_iterators, bool _Unique_keys>
struct _Hashtable_traits
{
    using __hash_cached = __bool_constant<_Cache_hash_code>;
    using __constant_iterators = __bool_constant<_Constant_iterators>;
    using __unique_keys = __bool_constant<_Unique_keys>;
};
We see three usings; understand them as three typedefs, meaning in order: whether the hash code is cached, whether the iterators are constant, and whether the keys are unique. Looking back up, what is passed in are three template parameters — false, false, true — which also confirms that unordered_map has unique keys, while the corresponding unordered_multimap has non-unique keys, its last parameter being false. We flip to the corresponding code:

/// Base types for unordered_multimap.
template<bool _Cache>
using __ummap_traits = __detail::_Hashtable_traits<_Cache, false, false>;

To sum up, the analysis above shows us the essential difference between unordered_map and unordered_multimap, and also how a single underlying container implements two container adaptors in the source!

docs.title: 2.The essential difference between unordered_set and unordered_multiset
docs.text:
The analysis is the same as before; first look at unordered_set:

template<class _Value,
    class _Hash = hash<_Value>,
    class _Pred = std::equal_to<_Value>,
    class _Alloc = std::allocator<_Value> >
class unordered_set
{
    typedef __uset_hashtable<_Value, _Hash, _Pred, _Alloc>  _Hashtable;
    _Hashtable _M_h;
}

template<bool _Cache>
using __uset_traits = __detail::_Hashtable_traits<_Cache, true, true>;

template<typename _Value,
    typename _Hash = hash<_Value>,
    typename _Pred = std::equal_to<_Value>,
    typename _Alloc = std::allocator<_Value>,
    typename _Tr = __uset_traits<__cache_default<_Value, _Hash>::value>>
using __uset_hashtable = _Hashtable<_Value, _Value, _Alloc,
                __detail::_Identity, _Pred, _Hash,
                __detail::_Mod_range_hashing,
                __detail::_Default_ranged_hash,
                __detail::_Prime_rehash_policy, _Tr>;
We can see that what is passed to _Hashtable_traits is false,true,true. For unordered_set, a const iterator and unique keys are used; now let's look at unordered_multiset:

template<bool _Cache>
using __umset_traits = __detail::_Hashtable_traits<_Cache, true, false>;
Comparing the two again: essentially, unordered_set does not allow duplicate keys, while unordered_multiset allows duplicate keys.

docs.title: 3.Three conclusions
docs.text:
Now, with the previous groundwork, let's list the four container adaptors in turn:

(1) unordered_map 

template<bool _Cache>
using __umap_traits = __detail::_Hashtable_traits<_Cache, false, true>;
(2) unordered_multimap 
template<bool _Cache>
using __umap_traits = __detail::_Hashtable_traits<_Cache, false, false>;
(3) unordered_set

template<bool _Cache>
using __uset_traits = __detail::_Hashtable_traits<_Cache, true, true>;
(4) unordered_multiset

template<bool _Cache>
using __uset_traits = __detail::_Hashtable_traits<_Cache, true, false>;

After comparing, we conclude:

  • Conclusion 1: unordered_map and unordered_set do not allow duplicate keys, while the multi variants do allow duplicate keys;
  • Conclusion 2: unordered_map and unordered_multimap use iterator as their iterator, while unordered_set and unordered_multiset use const_iterator.
  • Conclusion 3: for unordered_map and unordered_multimap the key is the key and the value is key+value; while for unordered_set and unordered_multiset the key is the Value, and the Value is also the Key.

For the last conclusion, compare the following (look at the first and second parameters passed to the hashtable):

unordered_map and unordered_multimap: 

using __umap_hashtable = _Hashtable<_Key, 
std::pair<const _Key, _Tp>,
_Alloc, __detail::_Select1st,
_Pred, _Hash,
__detail::_Mod_range_hashing,
__detail::_Default_ranged_hash,
__detail::_Prime_rehash_policy, _Tr>;
unordered_set and unordered_multiset: 
template<typename _Value,
typename _Hash = hash<_Value>,
typename _Pred = std::equal_to<_Value>,
typename _Alloc = std::allocator<_Value>,
typename _Tr = __uset_traits<__cache_default<_Value, _Hash>::value>>
using __uset_hashtable = _Hashtable<_Value, _Value, _Alloc,
__detail::_Identity, _Pred, _Hash,
__detail::_Mod_range_hashing,
__detail::_Default_ranged_hash,
__detail::_Prime_rehash_policy, _Tr>;

docs.title: 4.Important functions of unordered_map
docs.text:
Initialization

In the constructor below you can see that unordered_map's default bucket count is 10.

At its base, unordered_map defaults to hasher(), which is H1, which is std::hash

unordered_map(size_type __n = 10,
    const hasher& __hf = hasher(),
    const key_equal& __eql = key_equal(),
    const allocator_type& __a = allocator_type())
: _M_h(__n, __hf, __eql, __a)
{ }
Next, test whether the default hash is used:

unordered_map<string,int> um;
hash<string> h;
cout<<um.hash_function()("hhhhhawq")<<endl;
cout<<h("hhhhhawq")<<endl;
Output:

9074142923776869151
9074142923776869151
This further confirms that the default hash is used.
